signal: Today’s strongest signal is that AI reliability and economics are being decided by boundaries around the model: data contracts determine where frontier APIs can run, long-horizon RL needs trainer–sampler fidelity, RAG adds its own safety surface, coding harnesses materially change behavior and cost, and inference schedulers increasingly optimize against physical thermal state.

stories.title: Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen tighten frontier-model use over data-retention and IP concerns
stories.summary: Reuters, citing The Information, reports that Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen Hamilton are restricting or considering restricting advanced models from Anthropic and OpenAI unless stronger guarantees are provided around proprietary data. Palantir has pressed Anthropic for an irrevocable zero-data-retention guarantee before broader availability through its software; Nvidia reportedly limits Anthropic models to less-sensitive work and uses its own Nemotron models internally; Booz Allen has barred Anthropic’s commercial model for proprietary cybersecurity work. Both Anthropic and OpenAI say they do not train on customer data by default unless customers opt in.
stories.whyItMatters: Enterprise model selection is becoming a data-boundary decision as much as a capability decision. For sensitive workloads, contractual retention policy, metadata collection, isolation, auditability and provider substitution need to be explicit architecture inputs. Teams should classify workloads by sensitivity, keep provider interfaces portable, negotiate zero-retention where required, and retain a self-hosted or isolated-runtime path for data that cannot cross a vendor boundary.
stories.attention: Very high — enterprise adoption is now being gated by enforceable data-retention and IP boundaries, not just model quality

stories.title: T1 trains a 122B MoE terminal agent for 300-plus-step shell tasks with verifier-backed RL
stories.summary: T1 is a 122B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts terminal agent trained with reinforcement learning in real cloud shell sandboxes for trajectories exceeding 300 tool calls. Its recipe uses verifier-derived process rewards, training on the exact sampled token identifiers with turn-boundary drift repair, and rollout-routing replay that records and replays the sampler’s per-token MoE expert choices during optimization. The authors report improving Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 43.8% for the base model to 64.0%, while reaching 27.9% on Long-Horizon Terminal Bench.
stories.whyItMatters: The important result is the systems problem exposed by long-horizon agent RL: tiny mismatches between rollout and training behavior compound over hundreds of decisions. Training on the sampled tokens and replaying MoE routing makes trainer–sampler consistency a first-class concern rather than an implementation detail. For teams post-training tool-using agents, reproducible rollouts, verifier-backed rewards and exact execution provenance may matter as much as the policy objective itself.
stories.attention: Very high — long-horizon agent RL is moving into real shell environments where training–inference fidelity becomes part of the learning algorithm

stories.title: RAG-Safety-Bench shows base-model guardrails do not automatically survive retrieval
stories.summary: RAG-Safety-Bench isolates retrieval’s safety effects by comparing four conditions: no retrieval, an oracle document containing the harmful answer, related documents without the answer, and random safe documents. Across five open-source LLMs, the authors find an inverse relationship between benign and unsafe capability and strong evidence that baseline model safety does not guarantee downstream safety once retrieval is added. For some models, even benign retrieved documents can increase unsafe generation.
stories.whyItMatters: A production RAG system is a new model behavior surface, not merely a safer prompt with trusted context. Teams need to evaluate the retriever, corpus and generator together under adversarial and harmful requests, and should treat retrieved text as security-relevant input even when the source repository is trusted. Safety policy may need checks both before retrieval and after context assembly rather than assuming the base model’s refusal behavior transfers intact.
stories.attention: Very high — retrieval can weaken safety guarantees even when the underlying model is guarded and the document source is trusted

stories.title: Same model, different coding harness: no universal winner, but cost and task behavior move materially
stories.summary: A contamination-controlled study ran the same coding models under vendor-native and neutral harnesses on a private suite of repository and post-cutoff contest tasks. The paired comparisons did not establish an overall accuracy advantage for either harness: Opus 4.8 differed by -1.25 percentage points and GPT-5.5 by +1.25 points, both with wide confidence intervals. However, task strata moved in opposite directions, some timed-out runs had already produced passing patches, and observed per-solved-task usage costs differed meaningfully between harnesses.
stories.whyItMatters: Model benchmarks are incomplete for agentic coding because the harness controls tools, prompts, context lifecycle, stopping and retry behavior. The practical unit of evaluation is the model-plus-harness pair on your repositories, measured by solved-task rate, wall-clock latency and cost per accepted patch. The paper’s own telemetry correction is also instructive: agent cost claims are only as good as the instrumentation semantics underneath them.
stories.attention: High — coding-agent performance and economics need harness-level evaluation rather than model-only leaderboards

stories.title: HeatCache makes GPU thermal state part of the LLM inference scheduler
stories.summary: HeatCache is a thermal-aware inference scheduler built on vLLM for chassis-level liquid-cooled GPU systems. It models each cooling loop as a temporary heat buffer, estimates request heat demand, and schedules work to minimize energy while satisfying thermal-safety and service-level constraints. The authors report up to 18.0% lower computing energy, 81.7% less thermal-throttle exposure, and SLO violation rates below 0.9% at ambient temperatures up to 48°C.
stories.whyItMatters: Inference optimization is expanding beyond tokens, KV cache and queue depth into the physical state of the serving fleet. At edge and institution-scale deployments, thermal headroom affects throughput, hardware aging and cooling cost, so the scheduler can no longer treat every available GPU as equally ready for work. The broader pattern is to feed energy and thermal telemetry into admission and placement decisions alongside latency and cache residency.
stories.attention: High — serving schedulers are beginning to treat thermal headroom as a first-class SLO and energy-control signal

takeaway: Treat provider data policy, agent-training runtime, retrieval layer, coding harness and hardware scheduler as separately testable components. Sensitive workloads need enforceable retention boundaries; long-horizon agents need rollout fidelity; RAG needs its own safety evaluation; model selection should benchmark the whole harness; and serving policy should incorporate energy and thermal telemetry.
